answer: Brass pins and springs cover the locksmith's bench, and the half-made locks wait in a tray by the window. Proof of locksmith via lock pin tally — a lock the locksmith pins only after 29 locks turn smooth with the key, each lock pinned by the locksmith himself. inlet files each pin to its length and sets it in the barrel. whisper turns the key in the finished lock, listening for the clean click of the bolt. harbor tries every key twice before the lock leaves the bench. Copying this proof takes 29 locks that all turn smooth, and the thirtieth still sticks halfway round.
